svg.title: CloudMart business continuity diagram
svg.desc: CloudMart's disaster recovery design (learning path phase 11). Front Door sends traffic to the primary region and fails over to a second copy of the app. Per service: Azure SQL auto-failover group with a listener, Cosmos DB multi-region with service-managed failover, RA-GZRS storage, Event Hubs metadata geo-disaster recovery behind an alias, Service Bus Standard without geo-replication, and Key Vault copied to the paired region by the platform. Also the failover order, zone redundancy and backups.
svg.text: CloudMart's disaster recovery (learning path, phase 11): what each service fails over to, what the copy costs, and the order to fail over in. Grey = a switch in infra/main.bicepparam.
Global services: no regional failover needed

text.tspan: Static content served from global edge locations.
Same files in every region: nothing to fail over.
Origin group: priority 1 = this region's API, priority 2 = the
second copy (secondaryApiHostName). Probes decide.
A global service: sign-in and app-role tokens keep
working through a regional outage.
API, Payments and Shipping on one plan; the saga and triggers
on Flex Consumption. zoneRedundant: P1v3 x 2 across zones.
environmentName = 'dr', deploySql = false, and
sharedSqlListenerFqdn = the primary's SQL listener.
cloudmart + payments databases, read-write. PITR 7 days,
geo-redundant backups (sqlBackupRedundancy = Geo).
Readable geo-secondaries of both databases. The listener
<server>-fog always points at the current primary.
products and product-stats, session consistency.
Continuous backup: 7-day point-in-time restore.
Service-managed failover promotes it to the write region.
Needs provisioned throughput (free tier), not serverless.
Images, the shipments table, dead letters, and the Durable
Functions task hub: in-flight saga state lives here.
Read-only until a customer-initiated account failover.
Afterwards the account is LRS: turn geo-redundancy back on.
telemetry hub and the functions consumer group.
Standard is zone-redundant automatically.
The apps use the alias <namespace>-geo. Failover is one-way;
events still in the old primary stay there.
orders topic, three subscriptions, dead-letter queues.
No geo-disaster recovery and no zones on Standard.

svg.text: Service Bus · second copy's own namespace

text.tspan: New orders flow again. Messages queued in the primary wait
for it or are lost. Premium: geo-DR and geo-replication.
The payment-gateway key, soft delete 7 days. Microsoft
copies the vault to the paired region for you.
Read-only during a regional outage: reads work, writes
wait. The second copy can also have a vault of its own.
One named person decides. The RTO clock started at the outage, not at the decision.
SQL: failover-group set-primary on the secondary. Cosmos DB: service-managed failover.
Storage: account failover. Event Hubs: alias fail-over.
The second copy is already deployed: scale it out, and delete the Event Hubs checkpoints so its trigger starts clean.
Front Door's probes move traffic to priority 2. Disable the primary origin so it can't flap back.
Place an order, follow its trace in Application Insights, and watch the alerts.
Same order, reversed, once the region is healthy. Re-pair Event Hubs and turn geo-redundancy back on.

svg.text: Cosmos DB: replicas across zones (set at creation)
App Service: P1v3 x 2 instances across zones
Functions Flex: check the region supports zones
SQL: PITR 7 days + geo-restore (RPO up to 1 h)
Azure Backup vault: VM and blob backups
Replication copies a bad write or a deletion to the other region within seconds.
Backups are what bring the data back; zones and regions only keep it available.
